featured_reviews.review_text:
My detailed review of DG RUPAREL college

Campus(4.5/5): It's a pretty good campus as the ground is good but gets worse during rainy season so be careful of that . A volleyball court which is good too. Pretty good greenery all over the campus.

Places to chill(3.5/5): total 3 places are there for a group to sit properly one is named as Sawali which is just beside junior college staff room another one is Rupangan which is on the other end of the ground which is decent in terms of chilling and the last one is the banyan tree which is near the back gate of the college . If anyone wishes to play games near these places beware as the watchmen comes to take your id card if he sees you playing .(Places to worry are Rupangan and Banyan tree , sawali is safe )

Attendance (4/5): Attendance they say is compulsory and all but don't listen to them they are just bluffing just try to attend maximum number of practicals and submissions on time even for 12th lecture Attendance is not there .

Facilities(2/5): Facilities are not so great here the toilets aren't well maintained for boys it's okay but for girls idk but I think it'll be not so good . Other than that the ground for playing and all yes you can play on the ground only after you get your id card and have to ask in the office if playing on ground is allowed or not just to be on the safer side the timings for that are 3-6 only in the afternoon(if you are not from the college sports team for those students) . Classrooms are below decent sometimes it's as the infrastructure and all the benches tables fans etc are really old .

Crowd(3/5): Everyone will have different crowd preferences and they can get their type of crowd for being frnds as all types of people are in the college as for the seniors my personal experience was that as long as you are profitable to them they are good to you once your purpose is done they won't recognise you and all so don't look up to them if you want to socialize be a volunteer during ganpati festival and all and then you can be with them if you want .

Faculty(1/5): Idk abt com and arts but for sci the faculty is not good as they don't care much abt students and are not cooperating might even make fun of you in cases to look cool and all for cs branch in jr college there are 3 teachers out of which 1 is very very good and also personally clears your doubts and all 2 is good but very strict abt things she clears your doubts helps you too but she is a bit strict and the 3rd one is the most hated as she doesn't know what she is doing a lot of times she seems clueless and teaching also not good

Festivals: No such things as festivals but there are days around dec I think which lasts for 5-6 different days like saree day tie day etc and no freshers for newcomers if you are hoping from college if you want freshers there is an unofficial one organised by student council which requires ₹1000 per person and tbh it's total waste of money they promise unlimited food but it finishes after the 3rd round and no trips from college side again unofficial trip by student council which requires around 17-18k per person

Boards perspective (4/5): Teachers manage your marks in the internals help you during practicals and if you manage to stay in their good looks you'll get out of marks in the internals just attend the practicals and clear all the submissions on time

Overall(3/5): a decent college if you want stress free attendance and internals during boards etc but if you want to live your college life like in the movies plzzz don't come in this college

featured_reviews.name: Khan Asim
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is by far the worst decision I’ve ever made for my education. If you are considering the BCA or BBA courses here, please read this before you throw your money away.
The Affiliation Trap (YCMOU Nashik)
The college markets these courses aggressively, but they fail to mention the nightmare that comes with the Yashwantrao Chavan Maharashtra Open University (YCMOU) affiliation.
Zero Coordination: There is a massive gap between the college management and the University in Nashik. For any small issue—be it hall tickets, marksheet errors, or exam dates—the college staff simply shrugs and tells you to "contact Nashik directly."
Outdated Curriculum: The BCA and BBA syllabus through this affiliation feels like it’s from the 1990s. It is completely irrelevant to today’s corporate world or the IT industry.
Management & Faculty Issues
Unprofessional Staff: The administration is extremely unhelpful and often rude. They treat students like they are doing them a favor by letting them study there.
Teaching Quality: For professional courses like BCA, you expect high-end labs and industry-ready faculty. Instead, we get teachers who just read from PPTs and have no practical knowledge of the subjects.
Placement Lies: They promise "100% placement assistance," but when you actually reach the final year, you realize that most reputable companies don't even recognize these open-university affiliated degrees from this center.
Final Verdict
Don't be fooled by the building or the "Bunts Sangha" name. This specific program is a degree mill designed to take your fees while giving you zero value in return. If you want a real career in Management or IT, look for a college affiliated with the University of Mumbai or a reputed autonomous institute.
Save your future and stay away!

featured_reviews.name: Kidoo Land
featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually never write negative reviews, but after studying in this college and seeing the experience of so many students around me, I genuinely feel people deserve to know the reality before taking admission here.

The college presents itself very differently during admissions compared to what students actually experience later. During counseling, students are promised quality education, practical exposure, workshops, photography, makeup, styling classes, industry learning, and many other opportunities. But once admissions are done, most of these things either never happen properly or are reduced to very short sessions that barely teach anything meaningful.

One thing that shocked many students was the lack of transparency in fees. Students in the same batch and same classroom were paying completely different amounts for the exact same course. It honestly felt unfair and unprofessional.

Another major issue is the environment students have to deal with after joining. Instead of feeling supported, many students constantly feel stressed, pressured, and unheard. Whenever students try to raise concerns or complaints, they often feel discouraged from speaking openly.

What disappointed me the most was how the college handled reviews. Students were literally called one by one from classrooms and asked to write positive reviews in front of staff members. Many times, students were guided on what to write instead of being allowed to honestly share their real experiences. Because of this, I personally feel many online reviews do not reflect the actual reality students face after admission.

This college may look attractive during the admission process, but please research properly, talk to genuine students privately, and think carefully before investing your time, money, and future here. Education should feel supportive and inspiring, not mentally exhausting.

featured_reviews.name: Dawné DWN
featured_reviews.review_text:
This college is one of the biggest scams disguised as an educational institution. If you genuinely care about your future, mental peace, money, and education, stay as far away from this place as possible.

The admission process is nothing but manipulation and marketing. During counseling, Diana ma’am will make endless promises and sell you dreams about exposure, professional training, opportunities, practical learning, workshops, fashion industry preparation, photography, makeup, styling, and so much more. They know exactly how to emotionally convince students and parents into taking admission. But the moment your fees are paid, the entire reality changes.

One of the most disgusting things about this college is the complete lack of transparency in fees. Students sitting in the SAME classroom, studying the SAME course, in the SAME batch, are charged completely different amounts. It literally feels like bargaining in a market instead of a professional educational institution. Some students are overcharged heavily while others pay much less for the exact same education.

And what education are they even providing? Most of the things they promise are never taught properly. Classes like photography, makeup, and other “specialized subjects” are reduced to random one-hour sessions just so they can claim they covered it. There is no depth, no proper guidance, no serious teaching, and no real effort to prepare students for the industry. Half the students are left teaching themselves everything.

The environment after admission becomes mentally exhausting. Mamta ma’am and Sunita ma’am create so much pressure and stress that students genuinely start regretting joining this college. Instead of helping students grow, the administration makes students feel trapped, unheard, and constantly anxious.

And the worst part? Whenever students try to question management, complain, or speak up about genuine issues, fear tactics start. Students are made to feel like their exams, marks, or even degrees could be affected if they create “problems.” Many students stay silent simply because they are scared of consequences.

This college does not just waste your money — it destroys confidence, motivation, mental health, emotional health, and even physical health from the amount of stress it creates. The amount of disappointment students experience here is unreal.

Please do not fall for the fake promises during admission. There are far better colleges out there that actually care about students and education. Even if another college costs slightly more, at least you will get professionalism, support, proper faculty, and an environment where students are respected instead of emotionally drained.
PLEASE DO NOT JOIN THIS COLLEGE

This is a formal complaint regarding the extremely poor and unprofessional support experienced during my spouse’s Online MBA program at NMIMS.
During the admission phase, the assigned counselor (Amita) was highly persistent in calling and following up for enrollment and fee payment. However, immediately after the payment of substantial fees, the level of support dropped significantly.
A critical issue arose when the exam registration link was not functioning. When we contacted the counselor for assistance, instead of providing guidance, she responded in an inappropriate and dismissive manner, stating:
"Main kyun aapko bataun? Aap kabhi mera phone uthate ho kya?"
Such a response is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about the professionalism and accountability expected from an institution of this stature.
To clarify:
• Students are not obligated to respond to repeated follow-up calls.
• However, once enrolled and fees are paid, it is the institution’s responsibility to ensure proper academic support and guidance.
• Denying or delaying support on personal grounds is highly unprofessional.
This experience reflects a concerning gap between the admission process and post-admission student support.
I urge NMIMS to:
Review the conduct of its counseling staff
Establish accountability in student support systems
Ensure that students receive timely and respectful assistance
If such issues are not addressed, it can significantly impact the trust and credibility of the institution.
